claims.statement: Each src/ format module is a thin adapter between the CommonRomfile trait system and one in-process backend: archive (sevenz-rust2 + zip), chd (chd-rs), cia (cia-rs), rvz (rvz-rs), wbfs (wbfs-rs), xso (xso-rs), nsz (nsz-rs), gdi (gdi-rs), xdelta (xdelta-rs), xps (xps-rs) and wux (wux-rs); no backend is a subprocess.

Every backend returns the literal string "built-in" from get_version() because a linked library has no runtime version to query, so no module's version can fail. gdi, iso and crc32 export no get_version() at all.

nsz::get_version() reports "built-in, no Switch keys imported" when neither the data directory's switch_keys.txt nor ~/.switch/prod.keys is present, since only compressing NSPs holding NCAs needs keys, so the gap is surfaced before rather than during a compression.

Conversion and export availability is a static list rather than a tool probe: convert_roms::format_available is a matches! over the ten formats convert-roms offers (WUA and WUX among them) and export_roms validates its own longer list adding GDI, ISO, NUS and WBFS, neither consulting any tool version, and import_roms dispatches a .cia without any tool probe.

Format modules follow a fixed pattern: As* validates and wraps an existing file (some by extension, as_xso/as_chd/as_riff/as_rdsk by magic via get_mimetype), To* produces a file and returns a wrapper re-validated through the matching As*, and compressed formats implement HashAndSize/Check by decoding into a temp directory and delegating.

progress::run_blocking is the single adapter that runs a synchronous, CPU-bound format crate on the tokio blocking pool behind a bytes progress bar whose length is the input bytes the crate reports consuming; a panic in the blocking task surfaces as "Conversion task failed", distinct from the crate's own error.

archive.rs edits containers by copying entries already encoded: ZIP rewrites with raw_copy_file/raw_copy_file_rename, and 7z copies whole surviving blocks with push_raw_block so pack sizes stay bit-identical, re-encoding only a solid block that loses some of its entries.

A rewrite that leaves no entries deletes the archive: replace removes the scratch file and the original when zero entries are kept, and ArchiveRomfile::delete_file then removes the archive file once it parses empty.

Appending to an existing archive preserves the original encoded blocks: create uses ZipWriter::new_append for ZIP and rewrite_sevenzip with an add closure for 7z, and the solid parameter is unused because one entry arrives per call (batching a game into one solid block is a documented TODO).
Rewriting a 7z preserves its codec: is_zstd inspects the block coders and re-applies Zstandard at the default level 19, so a zstd archive does not drift back to LZMA2.

ROM-container Zstandard is chosen only in archive.rs: get_archive_compression maps SEVENZIP_/ZIP_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHM plus separate 1-22 zstd level keys (default 19, RomVault's level) and 1-9 levels for the other codecs onto ArchiveCompression. sevenz-rust2 is confined to that module, whereas the zip crate also appears in download_dats.rs and import_dats.rs, where it merely unpacks a downloaded DAT archive and never selects a codec.

7z extraction decodes the whole block containing the wanted entry and drains entries it is not after into io::sink, because solid-block entries share a single stream; copy_files_between_archives calls ZipWriter::finish explicitly so a central-directory write failure cannot be swallowed by a dropped writer.
ArchiveRomfile carries each entry's size and CRC from the archive listing, so a CRC check of a file inside a container is answered without extracting it.

RvzRomfile hashes a disc by opening an rvz_rs::Reader on the blocking pool and streaming it through common::hash_reader instead of writing several gigabytes of decoded ISO to the temp directory; Check takes the extract-to-ISO route only when a DAT declares a header.

RVZ compression mapping clamps rather than rejects levels: RVZ_COMPRESSION_LEVEL spans 1-22 which only Zstandard accepts, so the level is clamped to the codec's Compression::levels() (1-9 for bzip2/lzma/lzma2) to keep existing configurations working, and RVZ_BLOCK_SIZE is stored in KiB, rounded up to the next power of two and multiplied by 1024 for rvz-rs.

ChdType (Cd/Dvd/Hd/Ld), read from Chd::open(...).info() by parse_chd rather than parsed out of any tool's text, drives everything in chd.rs: which chd_rs entry point runs (create_cd/create_dvd/create_hd/create_ld, extract_cd/extract_ld/Chd::extract), the destination format (CD to CUE/BIN, DVD to ISO, HD to RDSK, LD to RIFF), the chdman-compatible codec defaults substituted when a system names none, and the rule that a CD-type CHD reports size 0 and no data SHA-1, so Size and HashAndSize bail and Check verifies each BIN.

CHD parents are resolved by content rather than name: as_chd reads the container's parent_sha1 and scans sibling CHDs in the same directory, running parse_chd on each candidate until one reports a matching file SHA-1 (silently yielding no parent if none matches), while as_chd_with_parent takes a caller-supplied parent - chosen by transcode::romfile_as_chd from the database's parent_id - and bails on a mismatch. create_chd then opens the parent to inherit its hunk size and extract_chd opens through Chd::open_with_parent.

The CIA path is a cia-rs parse plus certificate surgery in oxyromon: parse_cia rejects a CIA without title metadata, lists the contents in file-offset order named by their content ID in lowercase hex, and appends a tmd.{version} entry; extract_files_from_cia unpacks without ticket and footer, then appends the 0x300-byte TMD cert and the 0x400-byte CA cert from the extracted certs file to the extracted tmd file.

nsz_rs is given load_keys as a lazy loader rather than a key set, so decompression (unverified) never loads keys and compression loads them only when NCAs require them; load_keys prefers the merged switch_keys.txt import-keys stored in the data directory, loading its title.keys too, and falls back to ~/.switch/prod.keys when that file holds only rights IDs or lacks a key; keys are CRC-verified so a tampered file is rejected rather than producing garbage output.

nsz.rs records the exact equivalence to the subprocess calls it replaced: to_nsp equals `nsz -D -F` (fix_padding true, verify false, strict false) and to_nsz equals `nsz -C -K -L -P` (solid stream, ldm true, level 18, fix_padding false), with -K inherent to the crate and -P only needed by the Python tool.

iso.rs is in-repo Rust (a port of bchunk), not a crate: it parses the CUE the way bchunk does and copies only 2048 bytes of user data per 2352-byte sector for the first track only, refusing non-MODE1/2352 and MODE2/2352 tracks and a BIN too short for the described range; it also hosts the vendored iso9660 reader used by import-irds.

xdelta.rs and xps.rs implement common::Patch, which is not wired into any production path (both wrappers and As* traits are allow(dead_code) and only their own tests call them); xps surfaces xps_rs::apply's optional warning as "Patched, but ...".

crc32.rs adapts crc32fast to both the digest traits and std::io::Write, which is what allows common::hash_reader to pipe any decoder's output through progress_bar.wrap_write and thus hash a stream (such as a decoding disc image) as CRC32.

The dependency table shown by info, the GraphQL dependencies query and the MCP status payload is one list from info::dependencies(), keyed by backend name (sevenz-rust2, chd-rs, cia-rs, xps-rs, xso-rs, nsz-rs, xdelta-rs, wux-rs, rvz-rs, wbfs-rs), with gdi and iso absent, and a failing get_version would be rendered as "not found" / a null version.

src/chd.rs owns the whole CHD surface in one module: the ChdType enum, the ChdRomfile wrapper caching size, data sha1, container chd_sha1, track_count and an optional parent_romfile, the AsChd and ToChd traits, the RDSK and RIFF wrapper pairs it declares itself (ToRdsk/AsRdsk, ToRiff/AsRiff), the ToCueBin/ToIso impls it contributes to traits declared in common.rs, and the private create_chd/extract_chd that move the bytes.

chd.rs crosses to the blocking pool in two ways: create_chd and extract_chd run their conversions through progress::run_blocking, sizing the bar from chd_rs::cd_input_size for a CD and from the input file's length or the CHD's logical size otherwise, while parse_chd opens the container with tokio::task::spawn_blocking directly because a header read has no progress to report.

The CHD settings vocabulary lives in the format module, not in config: chd.rs defines CHD_HUNK_SIZE_RANGE and the four strum codec enums (Cd/Dvd/Hd/Ld) that config.rs imports to validate CHD_*_HUNK_SIZE and CHD_*_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHMS, and the workflow layer reads those keys per system and passes them down to ToChd as plain string slices.

`as_archive(Some(rom))` lists every entry and keeps those `rom_entries` resolves: an entry whose path is the ROM's name or ends in `/<name>` (a merged arcade set's `<clone>/` subfolder), narrowed by the ROM's CRC when several match, exact name first; the suffix arm applies to every archive lookup.

wux::get_version never fails: it returns "built-in" when the Wii U keys file is present and "built-in, no Wii U keys imported" otherwise, and the ToWua and ToNus exports bail with "No Wii U keys imported" when the keys file that import-keys stores in the data directory is missing.

WuxRomfile hashes a WUX without writing a temp file, streaming a decompressing wux_rs::Image through hash_reader on spawn_blocking, and its Check extracts a WUD to the temp directory only when the DAT declares a header.

When asked to bundle, ToWua adds the newest update and DLC in the library to the disc: find_update_and_dlc scans romfiles of TMDs, keeps titles whose ID shares the disc's low 32 bits and whose high half is 0005000E or 0005000C, gives a title holding no ticket the one stored for its title ID, passed to wux_rs::to_wua_with_tickets, skips it with a warning when none is stored, and keeps the highest version per title ID.

WuaRomfile reports its disc's hash and size from the DiscInfo a lossless WUA keeps, without reading the disc, and its Check compares that with the DAT and then rebuilds a WUX in a temp directory, which wux-rs verifies against the disc's SHA-1.
RVZ is never scrubbed: rvz.rs's options() always passes scrub: false, no setting offers otherwise, and export_roms::to_rvz copies an already-RVZ source verbatim.

With zip 9 an entry's name and each file_names() item are fallible; archive.rs's listing and rewrite and download_dats's Redump extraction propagate that error with ? and take an owned String instead of panicking.

wbfs.rs writes a WBFS from an ISO with wbfs_rs::create and the Wii keys, and from an RVZ through wbfs_rs::create_from with an RvzSource wrapping rvz_rs::Reader, whose title_key supplies the RVZ's stored title keys so no common key is needed and no ISO is decoded.
rvz.rs loads the Wii common key from wiiu_keys.txt in the data directory (an empty list when the file is absent), and maps rvz-rs's MissingKey error to the hint to run import-keys.
